### Study B · Joining across two spent knots

Define a successful action as a **funded birth with a paying live parent on each side** of the individual shared name. Record each donor’s available loose names, distinct charged groups and unary remainder. The spent knots authorize eligibility through their physical holdings. A requirement that either donate an old bit fails under the two-holder limit. Suppress that one eligibility decision on the identical preparation to isolate its effect. Doubling the shared name is a separate structural intervention that changes arities and can change the state reading.

Prioritize the two adjacent ternary knots versus the same marked pair embedded in a three-knot path. Verify equal marked readings, payment on both preparations, and literal common ancestry or a proof of permanent separation. A finite replay ending without a meeting gives a lower bound. Repeat the two-knot forecast at arity four, where the unary fresh floor can expose a missed charge. Construct the provisional next holdings *before pricing the first births*. Fresh private names add no physical meeting. At a sole parity closing, one provisional live knot cannot occupy both sides of a separating name. These observations give a direct check for circular pricing.

For the recurring sources, compare proposals at ages zero **and one**. Either age can change the first prices. For the seven-knot source, certify an alternate physical route for every original shared name. Those routes persist as holders are added. For the 21-knot source, check the initial spent pairs and whether any two original donors directly share a name. From age two, both candidate spent witnesses would have to be parents of current newborns. They belong to the same preceding cohort and have disjoint holdings. With the first prices matched, this gives an induction for the complete recurring history.

Finally, distinguish extension of every old word from realization of every legal word at a new holder. Disjoint private fresh bits prove extension on nonclosing cuts. Full local projection needs a separate input-extension argument, and essentiality needs erasure witnesses. For zero-fresh parity, check the new equation in the old row span and record its redundancy explicitly.
